parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, facility ban, document rule or police targeting is documented; absence in this thin dossier is not proof of safety. Positive evidence is general LGBT visibility: first Pride in 2021 drew ~600 people including premier, governor and ministers, and courts/immigration gave an appellate equality holding recognising overseas same-sex marriage. That suggests a tolerant public sphere and functioning courts, but acceptance is documented for LGBT people generally, not trans people specifically, and was conditioned on restraining displays of affection. Constitutional omission of sexual-orientation protection, restored marriage ban, and complete silence on facilities, documents, custody, care and hate-crime recourse for trans visitors leave the core traveller exposures as open questions, not established protections. Per rubric, open questions and resident-facing gaps weigh lightly, but without documented trans-specific acceptance or working visitor recourse it sits a step below the 0.75 acceptance-with-protections tier.
